substeps.caption: Pressure control OFF before any pumping (it holds 150 mbar). Wash one vessel while the other keeps its overpressure: graphite seals leak, and a leak should pull argon, not air.
Furnace wash 1: pump to the gauge floor, about −850 mbar at Provo's altitude (−1000 at sea level): normal, not a leak. Then argon back in to +150.
Furnace washes 2 and 3, same again. O₂ reads nonsense under vacuum: backfill, then read.
Furnace washes 2 and 3, same again. O₂ reads nonsense under vacuum: backfill, then read.
Then the chamber, while the furnace holds its overpressure: pump to the floor, fill with argon, repeat.
Generator on, 250 °C, wash again: the target is moisture in new insulation and crucible, not the metal.
500 °C, wash again. Stop washing once O₂ is low and stable: ≤100 ppm, best 40–50 (the team has seen the low 20s).
Pressure control back ON at melting pressure, the furnace slightly below the chamber (130 / 150 mbar). Ready to melt.
